attempts.hypothesis: I believe this world punishes time wasted more than anything else, so I'm building a value-weighted trip planner with adaptive navigation and robust recovery on the first attempt.

Sites must be found systematically within the ±20m hint scatter zone using a grid search pattern, with GPS-derived heading correction to combat compass bias, so I'm adding a 13-point search grid, faster stuck-skipping during search, and guaranteed base delivery.
I believe safe, energy-aware waypointing and persistent local searches will matter most, so I’m adapting motion to sensor feedback and returning before the battery or clock strands a sample.

The first rover spent the mission circling without sampling, so I’m slowing the steering, using sensor feedback to adapt the drive, and searching around promising signals before committing to a return.

I believe the rover was failing to reach sites because weak low-speed motor commands and noisy pose estimates made it wander; I’m adding stronger feedback, safer navigation, local signal-gradient searches, and a strict sample-and-return policy.

I believe the rover was spending too long stalled or searching without reaching sites, so I’m adding adaptive wheel control, direct site sampling, bounded searches around hints, and stricter return checks.

The practice trace suggests the rover can move but its goal logic often settles into near-zero commands; I’m simplifying task flow, ensuring it always has a waypoint to pursue, and strengthening sampling and return control.

The trace suggests weak science signals are trapping the rover in aimless local searches, so I’m prioritizing hinted-site sweeps, GPS/odometry-based waypoint driving, and conservative sampling and return decisions.

The trace suggests obstacle avoidance is causing long loops before the rover reaches sites, so I’m slowing and bounding motion, adding persistent escape detours, and tightening site searches and return reserves.

I believe broad scans and unreliable waypoint progress kept the rover near sites without sampling, so I’m using bounded sweeps, direct site-relative sampling, feedback-controlled motion, and conservative return reserves.

I will use a conservative adaptive controller that maps local obstacles, searches around surveyed sites, samples only safely reachable values, returns by beacon when possible, and learns drive/energy characteristics from its own sensors.
